newsitem.title: India: India protests to Pakistan over drone aircraft.
newsitem.headline: India protests to Pakistan over drone aircraft.

text.p: India lodged a strong protest with Pakistan on Thursday, saying remote-controlled aircraft had made several recent intrusions into Indian air space.

The United News of India news agency said Indian Air Force experts were studying film of an incident on Wednesday when air force planes fired at a small, pilotless aircraft which had crossed into the western state of Gujarat from Pakistan.

"The Ministry of External Affairs lodged a strong protest with Pakistan's High Commissioner (ambassador) Riaz Khokhar against the successive intrusion into Indian air space," a defence ministry official said.
It was not known if Wedneday's aircraft, called a Remotely Piloted Vehicle (RPV), had been hit, the ministry spokesman said.
"There have been some intrusions in the last couple of days in the Southwest Air Command region by remotely controlled, pilotless aircraft," the spokesman said.
"We believe this is the first occasion such aircraft have been involved in such incidents."
Pakistan said no pilotless aircraft of its armed forces had crossed into Indian air space or had been fired on by the Indian Air Force.
"There is no truth in this allegation," a Foreign Ministry spokesman in Islamabad said. "There was no such plane and the incident has nothing to do with Pakistan."

Indian forces in the region of the suspected intrusion near Bhuj airport, 300 km (190 miles) from the Gujarat state capital of Ahmedabad, had been put on alert and were searching for the aircraft, the Defence Ministry spokesman said.
"We have taken suitable air defence measures," the spokesman said without elaborating.
The region lies between Bombay and Karachi near the Arabian Sea.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since they were carved out of British India in 1947.

Troops on both sides of the frontier regularly fire on each other in the disputed northern region of Kashmir, which was the cause of two of the three wars. The rest of the long border is closely monitored.
The Hindu newspaper said the RPVs which crossed into Indian air space had sensors and night vision devices for surveillance.

"The "live' data which they can transmit is vital for directing surface-to-surface missiles towards static and moving targets, such as airfields and tank columns during battle," the daily newspaper said.

The pilot of a Lufthansa jet reported earlier this week that an unidentified aircraft passed within 300 feet (90 metres) as the planes flew over Moga, about 300 km (190 miles) northwest of New Delhi near the Pakistan border, an official of the Air Traffic Controllers' Guild told Reuters.
A Lufthansa spokesman in Frankfurt confirmed that one of its Boeing 747-200s had had a near miss over northern India last Saturday en route from Delhi to Frankfurt.
He said he could not confirm that the other aircraft was unmanned.
